summary: John M. Koller works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena and Charles Alexander Moore, and served as professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (attested 1988, 1999).

John M. Rosenfield was a scholar of East Asian art history, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. After earning his Ph.D. at Harvard under Benjamin Rowland, he taught at UCLA, served as professor at Harvard (1965–1991), and directed the Harvard Art Museums.

John Marshall worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at Cambridge and the British School at Athens under Arthur Evans. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1902–1931) and was an Hon. Fellow at King's College, Cambridge.
John Marston is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Washington in 1997 and held a post at El Colegio de México.

John Muir studied at Glasgow, the East India Company College, and Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1844, and founded the University of Edinburgh in 1862, where he held a post.
John Myrdhin Reynolds works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Rinpoche (~1971–1987) and Namkhai Norbu (~1979–2018).

John Nemec is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania, studied with Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher, and became Associate Professor at the University of Virginia (attested 2020).

John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. From 1959 to 1999, he was a research associate at SOAS University of London.

John P. Keenan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, held a fellowship at the Nanzan Institute (1983–1986), and became Professor Emeritus of Religion at Middlebury College.

John Peile was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, and under Theodor Benfey. He served as Fellow and Tutor at Christ's College, Reader of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1884–1891), and president of Newnham College.
John Pickford studied under Monier Monier-Williams and held an appointment as a professor at the University of Madras.

John Powers specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding positions at the Australian National University, Deakin University (2016–2022), and the University of Melbourne (2022).

John R. B. Campbell is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, also studying with Tenzin Gyatso and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

John R. McRae worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. After earning his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein, he taught at Cornell (~1987–1995), Indiana University (~1996–2005), and Komazawa University (~2005–2008).

John Ronald Newman works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

John Ross Carter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his doctoral work at Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith and served as a professor at Colgate University's Chapel House (~1972–2006).

John S. Strong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds and J. A. B. van Buitenen, later serving as professor at Bates College (~1978–2017).

John Shakespear was an Indologist and linguist who studied under John Richardson. He held an orientalist professorship at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809), and was Professor of Oriental Languages at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
John Shore was an active figure in Indology and history and archaeology. Succeeding William Jones, he served as President of The Asiatic Society from around 1794 to 1797.

John Stratton Hawley is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held a post at Bowdoin College (~1974–1977) before becoming a professor at Columbia University around 1986.
